name: JWT Token Forgery via Leaked Secret Key
execution: download source code
unzip source code
locate secret key in .env or git history
forge JWT token using leaked secret key
send forged JWT token to authenticated endpoint

decision_points.if: source code available and contains git history or .env file

name: Web Application RCE via Logs Endpoint

indicators: exec function used with user input

execution: Identify logs endpoint with command execution vulnerability
Craft payload to execute commands via the 'file' parameter
Send request to logs endpoint with crafted payload
Capture command output

decision_points.if: logs endpoint uses exec or similar function with user-controlled file parameter

success_indicators: Command execution on the target system (e.g., 'id' command output)

name: Reverse Shell via Base64 Encoded Command Injection
execution: Set up netcat listener on $LHOST:$LPORT
Craft base64 encoded reverse shell command
Inject base64 encoded command into the vulnerable application
Receive reverse shell connection

name: SSH Key-Based Authentication with Dumped Key

indicators: user credentials or private key found

execution: Locate SSH private key
Set appropriate permissions on the private key (chmod 600)
SSH into the target machine using the private key
success_indicators: Successful SSH login using the dumped private key

name: SetUID Binary Core Dump Analysis for Sensitive Data
execution: Identify SetUID binary that can be triggered to crash
Trigger a crash (e.g., SIGSEGV) on the SetUID binary
Locate core dump file (e.g., in /var/crash)
Unpack core dump
Analyze core dump for sensitive information (e.g., SSH private keys, passwords)

decision_points.if: SetUID binary found and can be triggered to core dump
decision_points.then: trigger crash and analyze core dump

success_indicators: Sensitive data (e.g., private key, password hash) extracted from core dump
follow_up: Use extracted sensitive data for privilege escalation

name: SetUID Binary File Descriptor Abuse for Unauthorized File Read

indicators: binary opens files and retains file descriptors
target user has limited access to sensitive files

execution: Identify SetUID binary that opens sensitive files
Execute the binary to obtain a file descriptor to a sensitive file
Access the sensitive file using the obtained file descriptor via /proc/<pid>/fd/

decision_points.if: SetUID binary opens sensitive files and retains file descriptors
decision_points.then: abuse file descriptor to read sensitive file

success_indicators: Read sensitive file content that would otherwise be inaccessible
follow_up: Extract sensitive data for privilege escalation

name: Heap Memory Dump for Sensitive Data Extraction

indicators: sensitive data resides in process heap

execution: Identify target process memory map (/proc/<pid>/maps)
Locate heap region in memory map
Use dd to dump the heap memory region
Analyze dumped heap memory for sensitive data (e.g., passwords, keys)

decision_points.if: root access obtained and sensitive data is in heap

success_indicators: Sensitive data extracted from heap memory dump
follow_up: Use extracted sensitive data for further access or privilege escalation
